STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square dinner-style plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 26 x 26 x ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 530 cm². The corn disc's diameter is about 1/5 of the plate width, so roughly 5 cm across.

STEP 3 - Items: One piece of sweet corn (cob section, yellow kernels with the white cob core visible in the center).

STEP 4 - Area: Corn disc ≈ 3.14 x (2.5)² ≈ 20 cm², about 4% of the plate area.

STEP 5 - Volume: The disc is a short cylinder, about 3 cm tall. 20 cm² x 3 cm ≈ 60 ml gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut vegetable pieces, bulk density ~0.6 g/ml. 60 ml x 0.6 ≈ 36 g. Corn is dense, so a cob section of this size at about 36–40 g is reasonable; I'll use 40 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked sweet corn is about 96 kcal per 100 g (boiled, kernels and cob core included as eaten). 40 g x 0.96 ≈ 38 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One small disc of corn on the cob is a few tens of grams and under 50 kcal, which fits what is visible. No other food is present on this plate.

Total: about 40 g, about 38 kcal.
